title: Editor does not reliably show extended script/class in "Create New Node" when using String path
body:
### Tested versions

I noticed this after switching from 4.3 to 4.4 however, I managed to reproduce it in both versions:
v4.4.stable.official [4c311cbee]
v4.3.stable.arch_linux -- package manager says 4.3-6

### System information

Godot v4.4.stable - Manjaro Linux #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Mon, 03 Feb 2025 16:27:19 +0000 on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated AMD Radeon RX 6700 XT (RADV NAVI22) - AMD Ryzen 5 3600 6-Core Processor (12 threads)

### Issue description

### When extending a script using a _String path_ ("extends base.gd") and setting class_name, the editor does not reliably show the extended script in the "Create New Node" dialog _when the script is in a sub-directory of the project_
**(for example in a "scripts" folder or in the "addons" folder)**
### --> When both scripts are moved to the project root folder (under res://), the dialog correctly shows both scripts


**NOTE**: Scripts both "compille" and work fine if attached to a Node via "Attach script" - the editor does not complain about them either, **it seems to possibly be a problem only with the "Create New Node" dialog**

**NOTE**: Absolute paths work
--> "**extends res://scripts/base.gd**" works
--> "**extends base.gd**" does not work even if in the same directory
--> "**extends ./base.gd**" does not work even if in the same directory

**SIDE NOTE**: In one of my projects which contains scripts like this, I get an assertion when I open the "Create New Node" dialog:
**ERROR: editor/create_dialog.cpp:297 - Condition "inherits == StringName()" is true.**
It only seems to appear in the 4.4 version, I dont get the assertion in 4.3
I also dont get the assertion in a fresh project

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a directory to store scripts, example "scripts"
2. Create a "base" script **in the directory** and give it a class_name
3. Create a script **extending the "base" script using a string path** ("extends base.gd"), **put it in the directory** and give it a class name
4. Open the "Create New Node" dialog, search for the scripts and observe that **only the "base" scripts shows in the dialog**
5. Move both the "base" script and the "extended" script to the project root folder (under res://)
6. Open the "Create New Node" dialog, search for the scripts and observe that **both scripts now show in the dialog**

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Can be reproduced in a new project, still including MRP just to be sure

[bugtest.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19183706/bugtest.zip)
